study_identification.title: Dissimilarity in Sulcal Width Patterns in the Cortex can be Used to Identify Patients With Schizophrenia With Extreme Deficits in Cognitive Performance

study_characteristics.study_objective: Apply a PBSI-based normative modeling approach to sulcal width (PBSI-SW) on longitudinal MRI data to quantify individual deviance relative to healthy controls and test whether markedly deviant patients show distinct cognitive performance and sulcation characteristics.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Outlier patients (PBSI-SW-Z < -2 at any time point; n=19) showed significantly lower estimated IQ at baseline and lower sulcation index at follow-up than nonoutlier patients; no significant differences in PANSS or medication associations after correction.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: A small subset of schizophrenia patients exhibited marked PBSI-SW deviance linked to poorer cognition and reduced sulcation; group trajectory differences were driven by these outliers.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: PBSI-SW trajectories differed by diagnosis (age×diagnosis F=14.57, p<.001) but this interaction was no longer significant after removing outliers. At follow-up, PBSI-SW was lower in patients vs controls (d≈0.36). Nineteen patients with PBSI-SW-Z<-2 had significantly lower baseline estimated IQ (mean diff ≈ -9.7 points) and lower sulcation index at follow-up, while age, sex, PANSS, illness duration, and image quality metrics did not differ. Baseline-to-follow-up scanner consistency was maintained and QC steps excluded poor-quality scans.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Outlier subgroup was small, limiting power; IQ estimated from four WAIS-III subtests; potential subtle imaging quality or medication effects cannot be fully ruled out; lack of external/multisite validation; limited developmental/premorbid data.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: PBSI-based normative profiling may aid neuroimaging-driven subgrouping; immediate clinical utility is limited but may support stratification in larger/multicenter cohorts. R code for PBSI-SW available on GitHub.

general_notes.general_notes: Initial total scans reported as 912 (Table 1 note); after QA and selection, 656 scans used. Scanner distribution per Table 1 (patients 81/83; controls 55/109). Subjects scanned on same scanner across time points. PBSI-CT analyses showed no group differences and served as comparison.
